clue.text: Bottle fell on lecher

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another sits after it, so the hide word follows the lecher word

parts.note: a goat is a byword for a lustful man
fell is an old word for an animal's hide or skin

explanation.surface: A drunken womaniser takes a tumble onto a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: a wineskin. 'fell' is not a tumble but the noun for a hide, and 'on' puts it after GOAT in this across light.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine and water were traditionally carried in a container sewn from the hide of a goat.

clue.text: The Cyclops sang it originally

definitions.note: the clue uses the name for the race of one-eyed creatures, a plural

indicators.note: originally hints that the letters come in an inventive, original order

explanation.surface: The one-eyed monster first performed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like 'at first', but here it rearranges SANG IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclopes of Greek myth were a race of one-eyed monstrous beings of enormous size.

clue.text: After a second, decided to find out

indicators.note: After places the decided word behind the letters for a and second

parts.note: certain means settled or decided

explanation.surface: After a moment's thought, someone resolved to investigate.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact is to discover it with certainty.

clue.text: Pin to the wall and rob

definitions.meaning: to fix something up on a wall
a hold-up, robbing someone at gunpoint

explanation.surface: Nail it up and then commit a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: As written it is a noun, an armed robbery, while the definitions read as verbs; the phrase as two words does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to post a notice on a wall and to hold up a bank or traveller at gunpoint.

clue.text: Suggest just ignoring the leader

indicators.note: ignoring the leader means dropping the first letter of the word

parts.note: simply means just or merely

explanation.surface: A hint that we disregard whoever is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to hint at it without stating it.

clue.text: But it comes not only in leap-years

definitions.text: But it comes not only in leap-years

parts.words: But it comes not only in leap-years
parts.note: the clue pretends to be about the extra day of a leap year, but a leap is also a jump, and the season comes every year

explanation.surface: Something that turns up in leap years, and in other years too.
explanation.walkthrough: The word can mean a leap or jump, so it 'comes in leaps'; the season also arrives every year, not only in leap years.
explanation.definitionFit: The season arrives annually, and the word is also a synonym of a leap or bound.

clue.text: Senior MP very intrusive in quiet resting-place

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: intrusive in means pushing into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a roost is where birds rest

explanation.surface: A senior politician is very intrusive in a quiet place of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MP' looks like a Member of Parliament but is the Military Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A provost marshal is the officer heading the military police.

clue.text: Idealised picture of a mother in one work

indicators.note: in puts the mother word inside the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
go means work or function, as a machine goes
ma is an informal word for a mother

explanation.surface: An idealised portrait of a mother within a single work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis the term is the unconscious idealised mental image of someone, especially a parent.

clue.text: Scotsman's crying at reception

definitions.meaning: in Scots, to greet is to weep

explanation.surface: A Scot in tears at a function.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots 'greet' means weep, and a welcome or salutation is a reception.

clue.text: Untypical work — a student does it

indicators.note: work as an instruction means knead or rework the letters into a new order

parts.note: L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: An unusual piece of work, the sort a student turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a noun, a piece of writing, but it is the instruction to rearrange A, L and DOES IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolated case is a one-off, not representative of the norm.

clue.text: York may be a curious choice, it appears

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the following letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Choosing York looks like a peculiar decision.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CHOICE IT APPEARS are rearranged. 'may be a' links the definition by example: York is one such office.
explanation.definitionFit: York is the seat of one of England's two archbishops, so its see is an example of an archbishop's province or office.

clue.text: Change vital old screw

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns or leaves turn colour
key means crucial or vital, as in a key witness

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter an essential worn-out screw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screw' is slang for a prison warder; the old word for a jailer who held the cell keys is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailer was once named for the keys he held, and 'screw' is British prison slang for a warder.

clue.text: View as one's own concern

definitions.meaning: a prospect or outlook seen from a high point
as in 'that's your own business', something only you need worry about

explanation.surface: Treating a sight as one's personal business.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a vantage-point prospect and, in the idiom 'that's your problem', a person's own affair.

clue.text: Extensive cosmetic surgery for pair in need

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: want means need or lack

indicators.note: surgery operates on something, so the letters of pair are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple who need major facial cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgery' looks like part of the cosmetic picture, but it is the signal to operate on the couple's letters; 'Extensive cosmetic' defines a slang noun for heavy make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is humorous slang for heavy, lavishly applied make-up, borrowed from the face markings of warriors.

clue.text: Men who fight at home put on trial and put in the cooler

indicators.note: put in tells us the cooler is inserted between the others

parts.note: in means at home
to try is to put on trial
a fan cools the air

explanation.surface: Soldiers tried at home and then jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cooler' looks like prison slang but is a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers are the troops who do the fighting on the ground.

clue.text: Not a long piece left after a deal is picked up

indicators.note: picked up means these letters are lifted out of the words that run together in the clue

explanation.surface: After a deal, a short leftover piece is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'NoT A LONg'. In card games, the cards left over after the deal form a stock players draw from.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the undealt stock remaining after the hands are distributed has this name, alongside its sense of a bird's claw.

clue.text: A view that's also held in the strangest places

indicators.note: held in means the word for also sits inside the rearranged letters
strangest tells us the letters of places are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A scene also found in the oddest locations.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of scenery taken in at a glance, or a painting of it.

clue.text: An example of top quality flowers and fruit

parts.note: flags are irises
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Superb flowers and fruit set the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' is not a river here; flags are wild irises.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's best product is its showpiece, named after the lead vessel in a fleet.

clue.text: Get going without a meal

indicators.note: without means the letter a is taken out

parts.note: to launch is to get something started or under way

explanation.surface: Setting off without eating anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text's stray 'IS' is an OCR artefact; the page has no such word.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday repast is a common example of a meal.

clue.text: Sound, completely ignorant over crusade

indicators.note: Sound tells us to say the next word aloud and write what is heard

parts.note: wholly means completely

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters of the word run backwards

parts.note: raw means inexperienced or ignorant

explanation.surface: Healthy, utterly uninformed about a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy but signals a homophone; 'over' reverses RAW to WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crusades were religious wars fought to recover the Holy Land.

clue.text: Petty swindle

definitions.meaning: cheating or fraud, used here as a noun for the activity

explanation.surface: A small-time con.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trivial, as in fiddling details, and also the act of cheating, from 'fiddle' as slang for a fraud.

clue.text: Pin smaller but very tight

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: A pin that is smaller yet fits very snugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk, and the answer is British slang for so drunk one cannot stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for drunk; this one means too drunk to stand.

clue.text: About to check about a reservation

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about

indicators.note: about means around, so the check word wraps the a

parts.note: to vet is to check

explanation.surface: About to examine a doubt or proviso.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning or proviso attached to an agreement expresses a reservation.

clue.text: Take a hand in ugly mischief-maker's hanging

indicators.note: in signals the hand letter goes inside the creature

parts.note: a goblin is an ugly, mischievous creature of folklore
in bridge the four hands are North, South, East and West, so E stands for one hand

explanation.surface: A gremlin's hanging, which someone should help with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' is not an execution but a wall-hanging: the Gobelins factory in Paris made famous tapestries.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry from the famous Paris works is a decorative textile hung on walls.

clue.text: The main fault, perhaps, may appear suddenly

definitions.meaning: the water main fault, a fractured pipe, is one example
as in to come ... onto the scene

explanation.surface: A main problem might suddenly show itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fractured water pipe is a typical failure, and to erupt into view is to come out abruptly.

clue.text: Imposing close in spa town (Georgian)

parts.note: august means majestic or imposing

indicators.note: close means end, so we take the end letter of spa

explanation.surface: A grand cathedral close in an elegant Georgian spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like a cathedral close, and 'Georgian' like the architecture of Bath; it means the US state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is in the US state of Georgia, home of the Masters golf tournament.

clue.text: Moving stair giving a lift to the top

indicators.text: giving a lift to the top
indicators.note: giving a lift to the top means one letter is raised to the front of the word

explanation.surface: An escalator lifting someone to the top floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving stair' reads as an escalator, but 'Moving' is the definition: the A of STAIR goes to the top of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and about, in motion or activity, is the sense.

clue.text: Man takes annual holiday without benefit — the patriot

indicators.note: without means outside, so the other pieces wrap round the benefit word

parts.note: he stands for a man
taken as written
a wake, or wakes week, is a traditional annual holiday in northern English towns
a reward is a benefit or return

explanation.surface: A man goes on his yearly break unpaid, like a true patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Wakes weeks were northern English industrial towns' annual holidays. The patriot is the Saxon who resisted William the Conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: This Saxon thane led resistance to the Norman Conquest from the Fens and is a hero of English national legend.

clue.text: Depart after throwing bomb

indicators.note: throwing suggests the letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Leave after hurling a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's 'hoist with his own petard' refers to this small explosive charge.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a small charge used to blow open gates or breach walls.

clue.text: A way of waxing poetic

definitions.meaning: a curved street of houses, a common British road name
in poetry the word is an adjective meaning growing or increasing, like the moon

explanation.surface: A manner of becoming lyrical.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a curved street, and in poetic usage means increasing, as the moon grows from new to full.
